description: The PxWeb warehouse root (px.bsi.si/pxweb/sl/serije_slo/) exposes only five top-level databases — Finančne institucije in trgi, Obrestne mere, Ekonomski odnosi s tujino, Finančni računi, Devizni tečaji tolarja — with no top-level 'plačila' entry. Payment statistics are nested two levels down as 10_denar_mfi > 95_spi.

result.result_summary: Payment statistics are discoverable only via the nested path, not from the warehouse root listing.

why_it_matters: A crawler that enumerates the warehouse root and searches for a payments database would report zero coverage for the single most important dataset in this cell. The collector must hard-code or tree-walk to serije_slo__10_denar_mfi__95_spi.

description: bsi.si appears to serve at least two URL shapes for the same material: a language-prefixed CMS path (www.bsi.si/sl/... and www.bsi.si/en/...) and an older/alternate unprefixed thematic path (www.bsi.si/financna-stabilnost/..., www.bsi.si/placila-in-infrastruktura/..., www.bsi.si/porocanje/...). Search results returned both forms for the same topics.

result.result_summary: Two coexisting path families observed for payment-system oversight and reporting content; which is canonical was not determined.

why_it_matters: Duplicate source records and false 404 'dead source' verdicts are likely unless the collector canonicalises across both families and follows redirects.

description: No dedicated landing page for the 'Poročilo o plačilnih in poravnalnih sistemih' series was located during this pass; it is listed on the publications index and individual editions were reached only via a media release and a third-party mirror (findinfo.si) of the 2021 PDF.

result.result_summary: Series confirmed to exist and be recurring, but its canonical per-edition URL pattern on bsi.si was not established.

why_it_matters: Automated per-year harvesting of the flagship oversight report cannot yet be scripted; the pattern must be resolved before scheduling. Not evidence the series is discontinued.

description: The metodološka pojasnila page covers financial accounts, balance of payments, MFI balance sheets and interest rates, but its payment-statistics methodology content is thin; the substantive payment definitions live on the poročanje/statistike-plačil instruction page and its attachments instead.

result.result_summary: Methodology for payment statistics is in the reporting-instruction attachments, not the central methodology page.

why_it_matters: Analysts looking for card/ATM/POS definitions in the obvious place will not find them and may mis-specify series.

description: Slovenian 'cash in circulation' as published is derived from the ECB capital-key allocation of total euro banknote issuance across NCBs, not from a direct national circulation count.

result.result_summary: Headline SI cash-in-circulation figures are an allocation, not an observed national stock.

why_it_matters: Using this figure as a proxy for domestic cash demand or ATM cash-cycle volume would be an analytical error; ATM withdrawal/deposit tables (ptts.px) are the better demand proxy.

description: All published BS payment statistics are national aggregates. No per-bank, per-acquirer, per-scheme-operator or regional breakdown of ATM/POS estates was found in any public BS source; the reporting instructions confirm entity-level CRD/ACC returns are collected but only aggregates are published.

result.result_summary: Entity-level ATM/POS and card data exists inside BS but is not published.

why_it_matters: Competitor-level ATM/POS estate sizing cannot be sourced from the central bank and must come from adjacent cells (operators, processors such as Bankart, bank annual reports) or a formal data request.

description: ECB SPACE, SUCH and the PSS/PTT statistical datasets appear to be published only in English; no Slovenian-language version of the SPACE report, its annexes, or the ECB Data Portal payment datasets was found in sl-language searching.

result.result_summary: Slovenian-language queries returned only Banka Slovenije relays and national media coverage (24ur, RTV SLO, Žurnal24) of the ECB findings, not ECB-hosted sl content.

why_it_matters: Collection pipelines for this cell must be English-language; sl-language monitoring has to be pointed at bsi.si rather than ecb.europa.eu, and any sl glossary must be built from NCB wording.

description: No machine-readable, per-country microdata or downloadable dataset for SPACE or the company cash survey (SUCH) was located — only PDF reports and PDF annexes.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced report HTML/PDF and annex PDFs; no CSV/SDMX distribution of SPACE country results was found.

why_it_matters: Cash-usage evidence for Slovenia must be extracted from PDF tables each wave rather than pulled from an API; budget for table extraction and expect 2-3 year refresh cadence.

description: The legacy ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (sdw.ecb.europa.eu) referenced in the seed brief has been superseded by the ECB Data Portal (data.ecb.europa.eu) with a new API host (data-api.ecb.europa.eu).

result.result_summary: All current documentation and dataset pages found resolve to data.ecb.europa.eu; no live SDW-branded payments page was surfaced.

why_it_matters: Any stored SDW URLs or SDW API endpoints in existing collection code are likely stale and should be migrated; unverified whether old links still redirect.

description: No page in this cell was actually fetched end-to-end during this pass; all URLs come from search-result metadata and snippets.

result.result_summary: Discovery was search-driven; liveness, exact dataflow keys (e.g. the PCP dataset code) and annex file names remain unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: Downstream deterministic verification must confirm URLs and resolve exact SDMX dataflow/series keys before any scheduled collection is built.

description: The FURS fiscal-verification open dataset (DAVCNE_BLAGAJNE_*) exposes only DATE, SKD activity code, invoice COUNT and AMOUNT. Searches for a payment-instrument breakdown (gotovina vs kartica) inside the published fiscal data returned nothing.

result.result_summary: No public FURS series splitting fiscally verified invoices by tender type was located; the ZDavPR definition of 'plačilo z gotovino' deliberately lumps cash and card together, so the fiscal data structurally cannot separate them.

why_it_matters: Any attempt to derive cash-vs-card share at the Slovenian till from FURS data alone will be wrong. Card share must come from Banka Slovenije / acquirer data and be divided into the FURS totals, with the definitional mismatch documented.

description: Searched in Slovenian for an official FURS register/list of certified fiscal cash-register software producers ('seznam proizvajalcev programske opreme za davčne blagajne').

result.result_summary: No authoritative public list surfaced across three query variations; only vendor self-declarations (Birokrat, MetaKocka, Minimax, Amstar) and interoperability lists on vendor sites were found. Slovenia appears not to operate a certification-and-publication regime for ECR software (unlike some neighbouring fiscalisation regimes).

why_it_matters: There may be no single-source census of SI ECR/POS software vendors; the vendor map for this cell must be assembled bottom-up from vendor sites, distributor catalogues and integration lists, which is slower and incomplete.

description: Looked for retailer-published, structured statistics on cash vs card share at the till (Mercator, Spar, Hofer, Lidl, Petrol) in annual reports.

result.result_summary: No retailer was found to publish a payment-mix table. The only quantified merchant statements located are indirect press quotations (Petrol ~50% cash; Mercator somewhat under 60% cash).

why_it_matters: Merchant-side payment mix in Slovenia is only obtainable via press quotes, direct enquiry, or association surveys — collection design must plan for qualitative extraction from news rather than structured reporting.

description: No public reference list of self-checkout or POS installations per Slovenian retail chain was found from either domestic (Mikropis/MikroPOS) or international vendors.

result.result_summary: Deployment evidence exists only as scattered press items (Mercator Tik-Tak since 2007; NCR self-checkouts for 12 SPAR INTERSPAR hypermarkets) rather than a maintained reference register.

why_it_matters: Terminal/self-checkout estate size per chain must be estimated from store counts plus episodic press evidence, so any deployment figure carries wide uncertainty.

description: No vendor press release or case study was located tying a named card-personalisation bureau (e.g. Cetis d.d., Idemia, Thales/Gemalto, Giesecke+Devrient) to a Slovenian bank card programme.

result.result_summary: The Slovenian-language query on card personalisation returned only Serbian commercial PVC-card printers and a generic OTP banka card page; nothing bank-grade or SI-specific.

why_it_matters: Card personalisation and issuing volumes are a direct proxy for card-statistics topics in this run; the absence of a vendor route means card-estate sizing must fall back on Bankart and Banka Slovenije data.

description: No Slovenia-specific Nexi or Worldline press release on acquiring or POS terminal contracts was found.

result.result_summary: Search returned only Italian, Polish, German and Spanish Nexi partnership announcements plus generic merchant-solutions pages; the Nexi press index remains the recommended feed to watch rather than a confirmed SI source.

why_it_matters: Merchant acquiring and POS estate ownership in SI stays undocumented from the vendor side in this pass, leaving a hole in ATM/POS data coverage.

description: The session's web-search quota (200/200) was consumed before planned queries on Payten Slovenija POS references and on Flik/instant-payment technology suppliers (incl. Margento) could run.

result.result_summary: Two queued queries returned a budget-exhausted notice instead of results; those two threads are unexplored rather than empty.

why_it_matters: Terminal-estate and instant-payment supplier coverage is thinner than it would otherwise be; a follow-up run should start from exactly these queries.

description: kontron-slovenia.com could not be fetched due to a TLS chain error.

result.result_summary: WebFetch returned 'unable to verify the first certificate'. The site is indexed with multiple live-looking SI-language solution URLs, so this is a fetch-tooling hypothesis, not evidence the source is dead.

why_it_matters: A significant SI integrator's financial-services reference pages remain unread; collection pipeline needs a browser-based or relaxed-TLS fetcher.

description: The most concrete Printec SI deployment evidence (first NCR SelfServ 27 ATM in Slovenia, for SKB) sits on Facebook and LinkedIn behind login/bot walls.

result.result_summary: Only the search-engine snippet text was observable; the underlying posts were not fetched.

why_it_matters: Vendor social feeds are where ATM installs are announced first; without a compliant capture route this channel yields snippets only.

description: No Backbase, Finastra or Sopra Banking announcement naming a Slovenian bank was found.

result.result_summary: The combined vendor query returned only comparison articles and unrelated go-lives; Temenos (NLB) and HRC/Hibis appear to be the load-bearing core-banking vendors visible from the supply side in SI.

why_it_matters: Suggests the SI core-banking market is concentrated on a domestic vendor (HRC/Hibis) plus Temenos, which is itself a finding but needs confirmation from more queries.

description: No source matching the brief's 'Bankazaveznik-type fintech commentary' could be located. Searches in Slovene for a dedicated fintech/payments commentary blog returned no independent Slovene-language specialist fintech blog with a stable domain.

result.result_summary: Slovene fintech commentary appears to be distributed across general business media (Forbes Slovenija, Svet kapitala, Finance.si), consumer-tech sites (Računalniške novice) and the ZBS journal, rather than concentrated in a standalone blog. 'Bankazaveznik' returned nothing identifiable and may be a garbled or non-existent name.

why_it_matters: The cell assumed a specialist independent commentary layer exists; if it does not, that intelligence must be sourced from association journals and forums instead, changing collection design.

description: Finance.si, the single most important business title for this cell, returned almost no full-text content through search — consistent with a hard subscription wall.

result.result_summary: Search results for Slovene card-business and fee queries surfaced Croatian and Bosnian outlets instead of Finance.si articles, suggesting Finance.si content is not indexed in full.

why_it_matters: The richest fee and market-share reporting is likely invisible to any unlicensed collection pipeline; a subscription is probably a hard requirement rather than an optimisation.

description: The Slovene term 'kartično poslovanje' is heavily dominated by Croatian and Bosnian sources because the phrase is near-identical across BCS languages.

result.result_summary: The seed query returned jatrgovac.com (HR), klix.ba (BA), banksoft.eu (HR) and a Split repository thesis, and zero Slovenian hits.

why_it_matters: Any automated Slovene-language collection must constrain by domain (.si) or add Slovenia-specific anchors (Banka Slovenije, NLB, Flik, bankomat), or it will silently ingest Croatian market data as Slovenian.

description: The Dnevnik.si business-section URL path was inferred rather than confirmed.

result.result_summary: Dnevnik did not appear in the result sets for the cash/ATM seed query despite being named in the cell scope; only the root domain is asserted with confidence.

why_it_matters: A collection job pointed at an unverified section path would fail silently; the path must be confirmed on first crawl.

description: Bančni vestnik full text sits behind a login ('Prijava') at bv.zbs-giz.si.

result.result_summary: Result titles for the journal archive read as login and legal-notice pages; the public ZBS site carries only issue announcements and an English 'About' page.

why_it_matters: The highest-quality specialist analysis layer is subscription-gated — this is a budget/licensing decision, not a technical blocker, and the journal should not be recorded as inaccessible.

description: No SI-specific KPMG banking or payments research publication surfaced in either English or Slovenian searching; kpmg.com/si presents financial services as a practice area but no report index with SI banking studies was found.

result.result_summary: KPMG SI recorded only as a pointer/watch-point with low usefulness; no report URL asserted.

why_it_matters: Prevents over-crediting the Big Four uniformly — for SI, Deloitte is clearly the productive one and KPMG/EY are thin.

description: No Slovenian fintech industry association publishing a market overview was found; the query for 'Slovensko fintech združenje' returned no such body. The nearest institutional locus is Banka Slovenije's Fintech Innovation Hub, which belongs to the regulator cell, not this one.

result.result_summary: No SI fintech-association aggregator source exists as far as this search could establish.

why_it_matters: A structural gap: SI has no industry-body fintech market report, so market sizing must come from foreign commercial aggregators (GlobalData, Statista) or vendor surveys.

description: No Slovenia-specific Visa consumer payment attitudes study was located; Visa's Consumer Payment Attitudes Study editions found are Asia-Pacific. Slovenian-language search for a Visa raziskava returned nothing relevant.

result.result_summary: Mastercard's Masterindex is the only vendor-run SI consumer payment survey identified; Visa has no SI counterpart found.

why_it_matters: Means the attitudinal series has a single sponsor, so sponsor bias cannot be triangulated across schemes.

description: Masterindex results have no stable canonical Mastercard Slovenia landing page in the results found; each wave is discoverable only through scattered SI media, SOZ and (historically) the Banka Slovenije National Payments Council e-news.

result.result_summary: Collection must be alert-driven across many domains rather than a single feed.

why_it_matters: A URL-based monitor would miss waves; the collection design must be keyword-based.

description: The Valicon homepage (valicon.net) was inferred from media citations rather than opened during this pass; no fetch was attempted, so its liveness and its publications-page structure are unconfirmed.

result.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence pending the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Avoids asserting a URL as verified when it was only inferred.

description: No Slovenian AVK decision specifically on interchange fees, card scheme rules or merchant service charges was located in searches in sl or en.

result.result_summary: Searches returned only EU-level MasterCard/Visa interchange material and generic AVK pages; the AVK decision archive surfaced non-payment cases. Interchange in SI appears to be governed directly by EU Regulation 2015/751 and handled at EU level rather than by national decisions.

why_it_matters: The expected 'interchange decision' evidence channel for this cell is likely empty at national level; effort should be redirected to AVK merger decisions and to the BS/EU interchange reporting instead.

description: No publicly published Banka Slovenije statistical series of consumer complaints about payment services (counts by type/provider) was confirmed.

result.result_summary: The BS complaints page (PUFS) documents the intake channel and legal framework; a regular published complaints-statistics report was not located in search results. Existence is plausible inside the BS annual report but unverified.

why_it_matters: Complaint counts are the core quantitative asset of this cell; if only ZBS/IRPS publishes counts, ADR data becomes the primary complaints series rather than the supervisor's.

description: ZPS comparator results appear to sit partly behind membership; full per-bank fee tables may not be openly retrievable.

result.result_summary: Public ZPS pages describe the comparator and headline conclusions; the detailed questionnaire-driven comparison likely requires membership. Not verified by fetch.

why_it_matters: Bank-level ZPS fee data may need a subscription or must be substituted by the Banka Slovenije statutory fee comparison, which is fully open.

description: No dedicated Slovenian financial ombudsman for banking was found; the function is split between Banka Slovenije (supervisory complaints) and ZBS (ADR).

result.result_summary: Searches for an ombudsman on fees/access returned the general human-rights Ombudsman (Varuh) and the ZBS ADR body. No sector-specific financial ombudsman institution surfaced.

why_it_matters: Collection design should not assume a single ombudsman dataset; the complaints picture must be assembled from BS + ZBS + TIRS + courts.

description: TIRS annual/business report landing URL on gov.si was not directly confirmed in results; only aggregate figures were quoted by secondary pages.

result.result_summary: 2023 figures (13,324 inspections, 6,587 measures) appeared via secondary summarisation; the canonical gov.si report URL was not returned by search and remains to be located.

why_it_matters: The TIRS candidate is recorded at the organisation root URL rather than a direct report link; a follow-up pass must resolve the actual report path before automated collection.

description: No Slovenian banking/payments industry AWARD programme was identified. Searches in both sl ('nagrada banka leta') and en (fintech/payments award Slovenia winner) returned only international award schemes (Juniper Research Future Digital Awards, Finastra showcase) and generic fintech listicles, plus the BSI Fintech Innovation Hub — none of which is a Slovenian awards programme.

result.result_summary: Awards sub-channel is effectively empty for SI banking-payments on the evidence gathered; hackathons and conferences carry the signal instead.

why_it_matters: Awards were named in the cell definition as an early-signal channel. If no national award exists, effort should be reallocated to conference agendas and hiring rather than repeatedly re-searching for awards.

description: MojeDelo.com, the job board explicitly named in the query, did not appear in results; only Zaposlitev.net, Optius, BorzaDela and the state ESS register surfaced. MojeDelo may still be live and simply not ranked — this is not evidence it is dead.

result.result_summary: MojeDelo not confirmed as a usable source in this pass; treat as unverified rather than absent.

why_it_matters: A missing aggregator could mean missed bank vacancies; needs a direct site check next pass.

description: The session's WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted before two planned queries could run: (a) NLB/OTP/Intesa/SKB careers pages and their LinkedIn hiring signals in sl, and (b) the SI/regional fintech event circuit in en (PODIM, Startup Slovenija, regional payments conferences). No fetches of individual pages were performed either.

result.result_summary: Coverage of issuer-bank careers pages and the English-language regional event circuit is incomplete.

why_it_matters: The largest Slovenian issuers (NLB aside from its hackathon, OTP/Nova KBM, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, SKB, Addiko, Sberbank-successor) are the biggest single source of hiring weak signals and are currently under-covered in this slice.

description: No URL in this slice was fetched or liveness-tested; all were observed only as search-engine results. The Bancni vestnik e-archive shows a 'Prijava' (login) layer and LinkedIn is behind a partial login wall — both recorded as hypotheses, not verdicts.

result.result_summary: All access_status values are inferred from result metadata, not confirmed.

why_it_matters: The downstream deterministic verification pass must treat every entry as unverified.

description: NIJZ (Nacionalni inštitut za javno zdravje) was named in the cell definition but is a public-health institute; no payment, retail-turnover or e-commerce statistics were identified in its remit during this scouting pass.

result.result_summary: No NIJZ dataset relevant to payment demand denominators was found. NIJZ appears to be included in the cell only as a stylistic example of 'AJPES-style official national statistics', not as a genuine source.

why_it_matters: Spending further collection effort on NIJZ would be wasted; AJPES and FURS are the correct non-SURS official-register members of this cell.

description: Searched in Slovenian for published FURS statistics broken down by payment method (cash vs card) derived from the davčne blagajne fiscalisation system.

result.result_summary: Found the legal framework and taxpayer guidance confirming that card and cash receipts are both fiscalised, but found no public statistical release aggregating receipts by payment instrument.

why_it_matters: This would be the highest-resolution national cash-vs-card measure in existence for Slovenia. Its apparent non-publication means the cash/card split must be inferred from ICT survey self-reports and central-bank statistics instead, or requested formally.

description: AJPES JOLP, the statutory annual-report repository, was assessed for automated collection feasibility.

result.result_summary: Documentation states free registration is required and a hard limit of 20 business subjects per user account per day applies, explicitly to protect the information system.

why_it_matters: Any collection design that assumes bulk retrieval of Slovenian company financials from AJPES will fail and may be treated as abuse. A curated watchlist approach is required.

description: Searched in Slovenian for SURS-published measures of bank-account ownership or financial exclusion at household level.

result.result_summary: EU-SILC covers income, poverty, deprivation and indebtedness, and an ad-hoc 2008 module addressed debt and financial exclusion, but no recurring official SURS indicator of account/card ownership was identified.

why_it_matters: Financial-inclusion denominators for Slovenia will have to come from the central bank or supranational sources (e.g. World Bank Findex, ECB), not the national statistical office. This is a genuine boundary of this coverage cell.

description: Searched in both Slovenian and English for a register or licence list specific to ATM deployers or POS terminal operators in Slovenia (bankomati, neodvisni upravljavec bankomatov, POS terminali, upravljavec bankomatske mreže).

result.result_summary: No Slovenian register of ATM deployers or POS/terminal operators was found. Banka Slovenije registers cover licensed PSPs, EMIs, AISPs and payment system operators, but independent ATM deployment and terminal servicing are not separately licensed or enumerated. These actors are only discoverable indirectly, via SKD-activity sweeps in the AJPES business register plus press and self-disclosure.

why_it_matters: The cell's promise to enumerate 'independent ATM deployers and card acquirers' cannot be met from a single register; it requires a constructed list, so downstream cells must not assume the register lists are exhaustive of the ATM/POS landscape.

description: Read the Banka Slovenije 'Register subjektov nadzora' page looking for CSV/XLSX/API export of the ~372 supervised entities across its 14+ categories.

result.result_summary: Only a searchable/filterable HTML directory was observed; no export control or documented API was visible on the page.

why_it_matters: Collection of the authoritative national licence list will require HTML parsing with category-parameter iteration and change-diffing, which is more brittle and needs monitoring for site redesigns.

description: Checked whether the AJPES beneficial ownership register (RDL/eRDL) remains publicly searchable for ownership mapping of small PSPs and ATM/POS firms.

result.result_summary: Multiple Slovenian sources report that from 09.08.2025 access was substantially narrowed following ZPPDFT-1 amendments, restricting the circle of permitted accessors.

why_it_matters: Ownership mapping must fall back to ePRS founder/partner data and court-register filings; planning a collection routine around RDL would be legally unsound.

description: Assessed whether AJPES JOLP can support bulk harvesting of PSP financial statements.

result.result_summary: JOLP documentation states free registration is required and imposes a daily limit of 20 business subjects per username, with larger volumes to be arranged via info@ajpes.si.

why_it_matters: Any plan to sweep hundreds of entities' accounts must either be spread over weeks, negotiated with AJPES, or restricted to a curated shortlist. This should be decided before the collection phase starts.

description: Root URLs for the commercial aggregators bizi.si and gvin.com were inferred from their service names; search results described the services and their pricing but did not return the homepage URLs directly.

result.result_summary: Service existence, data scope and pricing tiers are attested by search results; the exact entry URLs were not confirmed by a fetch and are recorded as unverified hypotheses.

why_it_matters: The downstream verification pass should treat these two URLs as low-confidence and re-resolve them rather than marking the sources dead if they fail.

description: Slovenian-language searches for actual ATM award notices ('enarocanje.si obvestilo o oddaji naročila bankomat', 'portal javnih naročil bankomati vzdrževanje razpis') returned portal homepages and commercial bank ATM-locator pages, not individual notices.

result.result_summary: General web search engines do not index enarocanje.si notice detail pages well; individual notices were not surfaced. This is an indexing limitation, not evidence that such notices do not exist.

why_it_matters: Collection must go through the portal's own search/CPV filters, the OPSI bulk datasets and the TED API rather than through general web search, or ATM/POS award notices will be systematically missed.

description: Commercial banks in Slovenia (NLB, OTP, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, DBS) are not contracting authorities under the public procurement act for their commercial ATM/POS estates.

result.result_summary: Searches for POS terminal procurement returned only banks' commercial POS rental offers and terms & conditions, not tenders.

why_it_matters: The procurement channel will capture public-sector and state-owned-entity demand (ministries, municipalities, Banka Slovenije, Pošta, utilities) but NOT the bulk of the commercial ATM/POS fleet. Fleet-size inference from tenders must be explicitly scoped to the public segment to avoid over-generalising the market.

description: Could not confirm the exact CPV code family for ATMs/cash dispensers from search results; only 66110000 (banking services) and 79710000-4 (security services, used for cash-in-transit) were corroborated.

result.result_summary: Search on '30123600' returned equipment vendor pages and no authoritative CPV mapping.

why_it_matters: A CPV-driven collection filter is the most reliable way to harvest TED/enarocanje notices; the ATM/cash-handling CPV set must be verified against the official CPV nomenclature before the filter is built, or coverage will be incomplete.

description: WebFetch of https://www.enarocanje.si/ returned only the page title with no navigation, search or API detail.

result.result_summary: Page is very likely live but renders content dynamically or is bot-defended; treated as UNVERIFIED, not dead.

why_it_matters: Automated collection from enarocanje.si may require a headless browser or should be replaced by the OPSI/e-JN structured exports; this must be tested before committing to a scraping design.

description: No evidence found of a Banka Slovenije tender specifically for cash transport / cash-in-transit services.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced only CIT licensing rules, Eurosystem cash strategy pages and commercial bank cash-handling T&Cs.

why_it_matters: Do not assume the central bank tenders CIT publicly; the cash logistics chain may run through NLB/Bankart or long-standing framework agreements. Record as an open question rather than a conclusion.

description: Slovenian-language searching for an Addiko Bank Slovenija letno porocilo returned only addiko.si product, tariff and data-protection pages — no local annual report or local investor section was located.

result.result_summary: Addiko's Slovenian subsidiary appears to disclose only through the Vienna-listed group (addiko.com), where Slovenia is a reporting segment. Country-level branch/ATM/card detail must therefore be extracted from group segment reporting rather than a local report.

why_it_matters: Slovenia-specific card and network metrics for Addiko may be thinner and less granular than for NLB/OTP/Intesa, so segment-report extraction plus locator scraping is the fallback.

description: No FY2025 annual report was located for NLB in this pass; the newest NLB annual reports surfaced were FY2023 (sl and en), alongside a Q1 2026 investor news item and the May 2026 Investor Day page.

result.result_summary: Search indexing appears to lag the issuer's own IR index. This is an indexing/recency gap, not evidence that FY2024/FY2025 reports do not exist — the IR index pages must be crawled directly rather than relied on via search.

why_it_matters: Collection design must crawl issuer IR indexes on a schedule instead of depending on search engines, or the latest network/card figures will be missed by a year or more.

description: Nova KBM and SKB banka no longer exist as separate legal entities; they merged into OTP banka d.d. on 22 August 2024 with IT and product unification in September 2024.

result.result_summary: The cell's seed actor list ('NKBM/Nova KBM-OTP' and 'SKB' as separate issuers) is superseded. Legacy report archives remain reachable (otpbanka.si downloadfile.ashx ids; skb.si PDFs) but will not be extended.

why_it_matters: Any branch/ATM/card time series across 2024 has a structural break and double-counting risk; legacy domains should be archived before they are retired.

description: No machine-readable (API/CSV/JSON) disclosure of ATM fleet size, branch count or cards-in-issue was found for any Slovenian private bank in this pass; all such figures sit inside narrative PDF annual reports or on HTML locator pages.

result.result_summary: Collection will be PDF-text-extraction plus HTML locator scraping. Backing map/locator JSON endpoints were hypothesised but not inspected.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations on extraction cost and error rates for this cell; argues for a locator-endpoint reconnaissance task.

description: No periodic statistical 'bilten' (bulletin) with payment, card, ATM or POS volumes was found published by Združenje bank Slovenije. Searched the site's Publikacije and Podatki sections in Slovenian.

result.result_summary: ZBS 'Publikacije' contains only paid handbooks (interest calculation, UCP 600 / URDG 758 translations, EFCB textbook) plus the Bančni vestnik journal. 'Podatki bančnega sektorja' shows eight chart images (bank count, employees, balance-sheet total, ROA/ROE, loans/deposits) explicitly credited 'Vir: Banka Slovenije' — no payments/cards/ATM series.

why_it_matters: The association-aggregated payment-statistics layer that exists in some countries does not exist in SI; A4 payment/card/ATM/POS statistics must come from Banka Slovenije and ECB SDW, with ZBS used for positions and structure only.

description: Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije's payments content sits behind a member login.

result.result_summary: The TZS page 'Nacionalni svet za plačila' under /sl/vsebine-za-clane/ shows only a one-sentence description of the council; full material (positions on card fees, cash, POS) requires TZS membership or registration.

why_it_matters: The merchant-side view on interchange/merchant service charges is the least publicly documented part of this cell; without access, merchant positions must be inferred from NSP minutes and media.

description: No Slovenian trade association dedicated to payment institutions, e-money issuers, PSPs or fintechs was located.

result.result_summary: Slovenian-language searches for a PSP/fintech association returned only regulator pages (Banka Slovenije: register subjektov nadzora, ZPlaSSIED licensing, oversight of non-bank PSPs), the ZBS glossary and legal-advice blogs — no membership organisation for non-bank payment providers.

why_it_matters: The non-bank PSP layer in SI appears to be represented, if at all, through the National Payments Council (Bankart, Nexi Slovenija, Dinit, Petrol Pay, Telekom Slovenije as individual members) rather than through an association — so the NSP membership list substitutes for a missing PSP directory.

description: No published GZS or TZS position paper specifically on card acceptance fees / interchange for merchants was found in the public web layer.

result.result_summary: Both sl and en searches surfaced collective labour agreements, chamber organisation pages and general news, but no 'stališče' document on provizije/interchange. OZS surfaced only general supportive statements about digital payments and mPOS.

why_it_matters: Merchant fee grievances — a key A4 pain-point indicator — are likely voiced in NSP sessions and member-only bulletins rather than public papers; collection strategy must pivot to NSP minutes and direct contact.

description: ZBS's Bančni vestnik archive path redirects to a separate subdomain.

result.result_summary: https://www.zbs-giz.si/bancni-vestnik/e-arhiv returns 301 to http://bv.zbs-giz.si/bancni-vestnik//e-arhiv (note doubled slash, and http rather than https on the Location header).

why_it_matters: Collectors must follow cross-host redirects and normalise the doubled slash, or the journal archive will be recorded as unreachable. Not verified as a liveness verdict — recorded as an observed redirect only.

description: ZBS annual-report page labelling appears inconsistent with the linked files.

result.result_summary: The 'Ustanovni akti in poročila' page presented as 'Letno poročilo ZBS 2025' but the extracted links pointed at wp-content/uploads/2022/04/ZBS-letno-porocilo-2021_*.pdf; separately an EN 2025 report exists at wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ZBS-letno-porocilo-2025_angl_final.pdf, and an EN page titled 'Annual Report for 2025' lives at the /annual-report-for-2023/ slug.

why_it_matters: Year attribution cannot be taken from page titles or slugs; collectors must read the year from inside the PDF or from the filename, or the time series will be mis-dated.

description: No RSS/Atom feed observed on the ZBS news section.

result.result_summary: The 'Sporočila za javnost in novice' page offers year filters (2021–2026) and category tags (sporočila za javnost, odzivi medijem, novice, obvestila) but no feed link was visible.

why_it_matters: Position-statement monitoring must be poll-and-diff over the year/category index pages rather than feed-driven, raising collection cost and latency.

description: Searches for Bankart annual reports newer than FY2020 returned only the 2019 and 2020 PDFs on bankart.si; no 2023/2024 'letno poročilo' surfaced in search results.

result.result_summary: Only /wp-content/uploads/2020/04/ (FY2019) and /wp-content/uploads/2021/08/ (FY2020) PDFs located. Recent years may exist but be unindexed, differently named, or filed only with AJPES. Not verified as absent.

why_it_matters: The most recent processor-side volume and market-share data may only be reachable via AJPES filings rather than the company website, which changes the collection method.

description: No Slovenia-specific published transaction volume or market-share dataset was found from Visa or Mastercard themselves.

result.result_summary: Scheme sites expose interchange/fee disclosures for SI, but no country transaction statistics. Country-level card volumes appear only via Banka Slovenije and the ECB.

why_it_matters: Scheme-side SI volumes must be triangulated from central-bank/ECB data plus processor reports; do not expect a scheme-published SI volume series.

description: The relationship between the legacy 'Activa' brand and current issuance is only partially documented in public sources.

result.result_summary: Confirmed: Activa system created 1992 at Banka Koper, operated by Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, settled by Banka Slovenije; Activa Mastercard products still marketed. Not confirmed: whether the Activa clearing system is still live as a separate payment system or has been folded into scheme processing.

why_it_matters: Determines whether Activa remains a distinct data-generating rail worth tracking, or is now only a consumer brand.

description: No Slovenian-language Worldline or Nexi country site with SI merchant/acquirer disclosures was located.

result.result_summary: Worldline material for SI is English (global domain); Nexi's regional SI-relevant content appears via nexi.hr (Croatian). Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. has no evident customer-facing SI website in search results.

why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring for these two processors will have to rely on business registers and press rather than their own SI-language sites.

description: No Slovenian public registry of merchant service charges (MDR) per acquirer was found.

result.result_summary: IFR Art. 12 requires acquirers to disclose MDR to merchants individually, but no aggregated SI public dataset surfaced. Only Worldline's SI scheme-fee PDF and scheme interchange tables are public.

why_it_matters: Acquiring-price intelligence for SI will require assembling individual acquirer tariff documents (bank price lists), not a central source.

description: No official, recurring public statistical release of Flik transaction volumes, values or user counts was found from either Bankart or Banka Slovenije. Every quantitative Flik figure located (approximately 776k-800k+ users, ~1.5-2 million transactions per month, ~EUR 126m in a peak month, ~90% still P2P) originates from operator statements relayed through Slovenian media or association articles, not from a downloadable dataset.

result.result_summary: Flik metrics exist only as press-relayed operator claims; no primary series.

why_it_matters: The cell's core indicator has no auditable primary source. Any Flik time series must be reconstructed from dated press citations with explicit provenance, and cannot be treated as official statistics. It also means displacement analysis versus cards/cash rests on the ECB/BSI credit-transfer aggregates rather than on scheme-level data.

description: No standalone Flik scheme website (e.g. a flik.si-style domain) was surfaced by either Slovenian- or English-language searching; all authoritative Flik material found sits under bankart.si (Flik Pay product and FAQ pages, merchant onboarding PDFs) or on individual bank pages.

result.result_summary: Flik appears to have no independent public scheme site; Bankart is the hub.

why_it_matters: Collection design should centre on bankart.si plus per-bank pages rather than waiting for a scheme portal. Absence of a scheme site also explains the absence of a scheme statistics page.

description: Only Bankart's 2019 annual report PDF surfaced in searching (under bankart.si/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/). A 2023, 2024 or 2025 Bankart annual report with BIPS/TIPS/Flik volume figures was not located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Bankart annual reports appear published but recent editions were not surfaced by search.

why_it_matters: Bankart annual reports are the most likely place for audited BIPS transaction counts. Recent editions probably exist and are likely reachable via AJPES company filings (JOLP) or Bankart's own site navigation rather than via search engines; this should be pursued directly rather than recorded as unavailable.

description: No published transaction counts for the Slovenian interbank e-invoice exchange (operated via Bankart) or for UJP's eRačun flows were found. UJP publishes a register of e-invoice recipients and a list of contracted providers, but not volumes; the only quantified view located is a survey report from EPOS.

result.result_summary: E-invoicing rail is well documented structurally but not quantified publicly.

why_it_matters: E-invoicing volume is a leading indicator for B2B A2A payment automation. Without it, the e-invoicing dimension of the cell rests on registry counts (recipients, providers) and survey estimates, which should be flagged as proxies.

description: No Slovenian aggregate statistic on PSD2 API call volumes, TPP counts or open-banking usage was located. Individual banks publish statutory API availability/performance disclosures and the Bankart HUB lists connected ASPSPs, but there is no national roll-up.

result.result_summary: Open-banking usage in SI is only measurable bank-by-bank or via the EBA/BSI licence registers.

why_it_matters: Claims about open-banking adoption in Slovenia will have to be built bottom-up from per-bank disclosures plus TPP licence registers, which is labour-intensive and should be scoped explicitly.

description: A Sberbank Slovenia PSD2 page (sberbank.si) still appears in search results although Sberbank Slovenia was absorbed into NLB in 2022. Similarly, Valú references found date to 2021/2022 and the current Valú product URL was not confirmed.

result.result_summary: Search results include defunct-institution and stale wallet pages.

why_it_matters: The ASPSP/wallet register must be validated against current licensing rather than search results, or the source list will carry dead actors. Note these are unverified-status observations, not confirmed dead links.

description: No evidence was found of Loomis, Brink's or Prosegur Cash operating a Slovenian cash-in-transit subsidiary. A targeted Slovenian-language search naming Loomis alongside domestic providers returned only domestic firms (Sintal, G4S Slovenija, Varnost Vic, FIT varovanje, IBS Varovanje) and no international CIT specialist other than G4S.

result.result_summary: The Slovenian CIT market appears to be served by domestic private security firms plus G4S, with no visible presence of the global pure-play CIT majors. This is a hypothesis based on absence in search results, not a verified market fact.

why_it_matters: Market structure and consolidation prospects for cash logistics differ sharply depending on whether global CIT majors are present. If confirmed, the Slovenian CIT segment is a domestic-security-firm market where cash transport is one service line among many, rather than a specialist cash-handling industry - which affects pricing, cash-centre investment and willingness to invest in recycling technology.

description: No source was found that publishes Slovenian ATM WITHDRAWAL VOLUMES or VALUES at ATM, operator or geographic level. Banka Slovenije payment statistics coverage surfaced in search focused on ATM counts, card counts and card payment volumes; the ATM-cash-withdrawal series was not confirmed as separately published, and no per-operator or per-municipality withdrawal data appeared in any local-language search.

result.result_summary: Estate counts are well covered; cash withdrawal throughput is not. The withdrawal side is presently only inferable from cash-in-circulation aggregates.

why_it_matters: Terminal counts alone cannot distinguish a shrinking but heavily used ATM estate from a shrinking and lightly used one. Without withdrawal volumes, the commercial case for or against maintaining rural ATMs - and the addressable market for deployers and CIT firms - cannot be sized. This gap should be attacked next via the ECB Data Portal payment statistics for Slovenia, which does carry ATM withdrawal series.

description: Searching did not surface a settled Slovenian term or any identified actor for CASH RECYCLERS or cash-recycling ATMs (candidate terms would be 'recikliranje gotovine', 'bankomat z vplacilom', 'vplacilni bankomat', 'depozitni bankomat', 'denarni center'). No Slovenian vendor, bank programme or Banka Slovenije accreditation list for cash recycling was found in this pass.

result.result_summary: The cash-recycler sub-topic of this cell is currently uncovered: neither terminology nor actors were confirmed in Slovenian.

why_it_matters: Recycling ATMs materially change CIT servicing frequency and the cost of rural cash access, which is precisely the variable the ZDUPS coverage mandate turns on. A blind spot here means the cost side of the access-to-cash obligation cannot be modelled. Explicitly flagged as a local-language coverage failure, per the mandatory-local-language rule.

description: The Bankart open banking hub's ATM-network API was identified from portal documentation summaries but the actual endpoint, its authentication requirements and its terms of use were NOT inspected. It is unknown whether the ATM locator is unauthenticated (as PSD2 location data usually is) or requires developer registration and eIDAS certificates.

result.result_summary: High-value machine-readable source identified but access conditions unverified. Not a failure - an open verification task.

why_it_matters: Whether this API is openly pollable determines whether the entire ATM estate can be tracked directly and lawfully, or whether the pipeline must depend on the third-party ATMinfo.si rendering with its unknown terms and unknown completeness (ATMinfo showed ~1,046 ATMs against ~1,284-1,304 reported by Banka Slovenije, suggesting it may not cover independent deployers such as Euronet).

description: Three different ATM totals were observed and are not reconciled: ATMinfo.si displayed 1,046 ATMs across eight banks; press citing Banka Slovenije reported 1,284 at end-H2 2024 (down 1.9 percent); and other reporting cited 1,304 at end-2025 for credit institutions AND independent providers combined.

result.result_summary: The gap of roughly 250 units is most plausibly the independent-deployer estate (Euronet and similar) absent from the bank-only aggregation, but this was not verified.

why_it_matters: The independent deployer share of the Slovenian ATM estate may be around 20 percent - materially larger than the bank-centric debate implies - and directly determines who the commercial counterparties are for ATM hardware, servicing and cash logistics. Reconciling these three series is a priority analytical task and would itself be a finding.

description: No Slovenian trade association specifically for independent ATM deployers or for the ATM industry was found (no national equivalent of an ATM Industry Association chapter surfaced in either language). Euronet appears to engage the market and municipalities directly rather than through a sector body.

result.result_summary: The independent deployer segment has no organised collective voice in Slovenia that could be tracked as a single source.

why_it_matters: Absent a trade body, deployer-side data and lobbying positions must be gathered actor by actor (chiefly Euronet, plus its parent's investor disclosures) and from municipal procurement records, which is more labour-intensive and less complete. It also means the ZDUPS consultation record may under-represent the deployer perspective.
